questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The movie Uri tells the story of a surgical strike by the Indian army __towards militants in POK__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3), i.e., Against militants in POK.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the incorrect preposition '**towards**'.

 
 
• As it talks about the '**strike**' by Indian army; the preposition should show this opposition/ conflict between two parties.
 
 
 
• **Let's look at how the given prepositions are used:**
 
 
• **Towards**- expressing the relation between behaviour and the thing at which it is directed. Example: He was always warm towards her.
 
• **For**- indicating the purpose of something. Example: The flowers are for you.
 
• **Over**- showing the trajectory or duration of something. Example: The people were scattered all over the mountain. 
 
• **Against**- in opposition to. Example: It is the job of the police to fight against crime.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Given the above context, only the preposition '**Against**' is appropriate here.

**Thus, the rectified sentence is:** *The movie Uri tells the story of a surgical strike by the Indian army **against** **militants in POK**__. *

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

They visited the Qutub Minar, which is most attractive spot in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2), i.e., Which is most.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The sentence uses the incorrect form 'which is most'.
 
• The sentence uses the superlative degree of adjective '**most attractiv**e', for the noun **Qutub Minar.**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• ** Adjective Rule: Superlative degree of an adjective is always preceded by the article 'The'. *Example: You are the best friend I have ever had.***
 
• So, here, there should be the article '**The**' used before the adjective. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using the article '**The**' gives superlative adjective the specificity of being the best, out of all others of its nature. 

**Thus, the rectified sentence is: ***They visited the Qutub Minar, which is **the** most attractive spot in Delhi.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. **

The furniture in this room __are old and need__ to be replaced.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e., Is old and needs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Let's look at the following points-**

__
 
• The sentence uses the incorrect plural verbs '**are **and **need**'; which is incorrect.
 
• The subject '**Furniture**' is an uncountable noun; so it is always used in its singular form.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement Rule: A singular subject takes singular verbs while a plural subject uses a plural verb. *Example: She goes. (Singular) They go. (Plural)***
 
• Since '**Furniture**' is singular, the corresponding verbs must also be the singular forms '**is**' and '**needs**' respectively.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e24eedc7cd1bcfcf3e585e6fa7a2d3c6804de35c8ec0ab58e1973f36d4c8546d.png] Extra-Bite:**

 
• When using the plural form of Furniture, we say 'pieces of furniture'.

 

**Thus, the rectified sentence is: ***The furniture in this room **is old and needs__** to be replaced.*

questions.question:
**Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate words.**

________ taught you such lessons as these?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4), i.e., Who.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c85df1d0885ef6fd1ccb6d6eeeb4f0ac2cb3339955502df2aa31deb31b5ead58.png] ​**Explanation**:

__
 
• The sentence is a question; so the blank must contain a wh-pronoun, which is the subject of the sentence.
 
• The sentence talks about 'teaching lessons', which can only be done by a person.
 
• In such cases, the pronoun '**Who**' is used, asking which person did that particular thing.__ ***Example: Who is your father?***
 
• ** Extra Point:**
 
• The use of pronouns in questions depend on their context.
 
• **What**- used to ask about a general something. ***Example: What is the matter?***
 
• **Which**- used to identify a particular thing from many. ***Example: Which flower do you want?***
 
• **Whom**- used as a passive form of 'Who'. ***Example: This was done by whom?***

**Thus, the complete sentence is**: *__**Who**__ taught you such lessons as these?*
